reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must accept END PROGRAM program-name. (period required, program-name a user-defined word identical to the PROGRAM-ID it closes, for a contained program and for a separately compiled program that follows), and refuse END FUNCTION, a missing or wrong name, a literal name, a missing PROGRAM keyword and a missing period; witnesses cover only the END FUNCTION refusals.

edition-consulted.switches: edition.Edition.Year >= 2002: whether a program with contained programs must have a procedure division (1985 prints separate brackets); not the end marker keyword or name
FUNCTION-ID definition (with its END FUNCTION) refused below 2002 (function-definition-2002)

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|Year|DialectLevel in SourceUnitShape.cs and EndMarkerPass.cs; EndMarkerPass consults the edition only as a diagnostic sink
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no for END PROGRAM itself; END FUNCTION closing a program is COBOL2274 at every edition, and the FUNCTION-ID unit it belongs to is a 2002 construct
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witnesses exercise END FUNCTION refusals only; the accepted END PROGRAM forms and the name/period refusals are not exercised

probes.printed: OUTER / INNER (contained program closed by END PROGRAM EPIN, then END PROGRAM EPOUT, then a separate program EPSEP)
COMPILED (END PROGRAM epx. closing PROGRAM-ID. EPX.)
85 and 2023: COBOL2274 END FUNCTION cannot close a program definition
COBOL2793 the end marker names 'EPY', but the program-name declared ... is 'EPX'
COBOL5506 unexpected '"EPX"' ... no literal is expected
probes.expected: literal not a user-defined word, refused

probes.printed: COBOL5506 missing token before 'EPX' ... expected FUNCTION or PROGRAM

reader.notes: The grammar writes END (PROGRAM | FUNCTION) programName DOT as a superset; SourceUnitShape refuses the FUNCTION keyword on a program and EndMarkerPass the name mismatch, both edition-invariant and correct at 85. Diagnostics at 85 still mention FUNCTION as an expected word (epr6), which is cosmetic.

refuter.evidence: At --std 85 vs 2023 (probes in E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-001/): ep_a.cob, a second program after END PROGRAM EPA. that begins with PROGRAM-ID (no IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header): 85 COBOL0900 'source unit without the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header requires COBOL-2002', 2023 compiles and runs A; cite.py OK  §1985:VI.2.4.4 GR2 ('it must be the Identification Division header of a program to be compiled separately'). ep_b.cob, first of two separately compiled programs with no END PROGRAM: refused at 85 and 2023 (COBOL2793; message says 'contains', slightly misleading, still a refusal) as §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2 requires (cite.py OK  §1985:VI.2.3.3 GR2 'must be terminated by an end program header'). ep_c.cob END PROGRAM starting in area B: 85 COBOL3734, 2023 compiles (1985 reference format: end program header starts in area A). ep_d.cob a duplicated END PROGRAM and ep_e.cob a statement after END PROGRAM: COBOL0001 at both. Edition sites the reader did not list (area-A check COBOL3734 and the IDENTIFICATION DIVISION header gate COBOL0900) take a correct 85 arm.
